newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen dipping.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend slight fall, seen dipping.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday fell slightly for the fourth straight session and analysts said the market should stay flat or slightly down for most of this week as investors take profits after the recent 38-percent surge.

"The flat-to-slightly-downward tendency should continue but we should see a return to growth after the market calms and some investors take profits," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Some analysts said the bourse would soon rebound as long as foreign exchanges stay strong, while others said it was not yet clear what would happen after the current slight downtrend.

The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 18,090.8 points and turnover fell 18.4 percent to 165.8 million zlotys ($54.5 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 39 to 35 with 15 stocks flat.

Analysts said February 11-20 food price data due on Friday would likely not affect the market as the central bank was waiting to see the results on inflation of its recent decision to raise banks' obligatory reserves before changing rates.
The move takes affect on February 28.
Analysts said biggest loser computer maker Optimus fell the daily maximum 10 percent in profit-taking after having surged so far this year.

Analysts said garment makers Wolczanka, Vistula and Prochnik, which rose 10 percent, 8.1 percent and 5.6 percent respectively, were rising after looking relatively undervalued after a poor 1996 on the bourse.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 0.6 percent to 167 zlotys ($54.9) in 53.9 million-zloty ($17.7 million) trade and rose 2.4 percent to 171 zlotys ($56.3) in 69.3-million-zloty ($22.8 million) live trade, where most stocks closed lower in 23.7-million-zloty ($7.8 million) trade.
